summary: Possible typosquat of @solana/web3.js under unofficial @solana-labs scope
details: Package name `@solana-labs/web3js` closely resembles the official Solana JavaScript SDK published as `@solana/web3.js`. The scope `@solana-labs` is not the established publisher scope for the Solana web3 client (which is `@solana`), and the package name drops the dot in `web3.js`. The shipped bundle (lib/index.cjs.js, lib/index.esm.js) contains keyword co-occurrences flagged by pattern rules — `require('child_process')`, `fetch(`, `POST`, `curl`, `ping` — but these appear in a single-line minified rollup that may legitimately reflect the upstream SDK's own code (the official `@solana/web3.js` bundle is large and references many primitives). Without traced-code corroboration showing exfiltration, hardcoded attacker C2, env-var scraping, or a lifecycle-time dropper, the structural evidence is insufficient to confirm an active attack. However, the scope/name proximity to a widely-installed SDK is a strong confusion-risk signal that warrants human review before publishing a verdict — a reviewer should compare the bundle against the official @solana/web3.js source to determine whether this is a benign re-publish, an old fork, or an attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
